input.question: How can airbnb inflate rental and housing prices; shouldn't competition drive down prices?
input.ground_truth: AirBnB drives down ***short term rental*** prices. AKA "hotel" prices. It does this at the expense of decreasing the housing supply and ***driving up*** prices for long-term accommodations like homes and condos. In a simple supply and demand equation, it increases the supply of SHORT TERM accommodation (like hotel rooms) - reducing their cost- and decreases the supply of long-term accommodations (like houses) - increasing their cost.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How can airbnb inflate rental and housing prices; shouldn't competition drive down prices?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine there are lots of lemonade stands in your neighborhood. Normally, if there are a lot of lemonade stands, each one might lower their price so more kids will come buy lemonade from them, right? That’s competition—it helps make things cheaper.

But let’s say one big company (like Airbnb) buys or controls many of the lemonade stands. Now, even if there are lots of stands, the company can decide to charge almost the same high price at every stand. Why? Because if you want lemonade and all the stands are run by the same company, you don’t have a choice to go to a cheaper one.

Airbnb can be a little like that with houses and apartments. If lots of houses are listed on Airbnb, the owners might think, “Oh, my house can make a lot of money!” and they all raise their prices. Also, if people want to stay in a city for a big event, and almost everyone is putting their homes on Airbnb, there are fewer homes left for people who want to live there. So, the homes that are left for regular living get more expensive too, because everyone is competing for the few available places.

So even though there are lots of listings (like lots of lemonade stands), the company and the owners can work together (without really competing against each other) to keep prices high. That’s how Airbnb can help make rental and housing prices go up instead of down.
